declared.title: Mental Simulation Effects on Performance: Benefits of Outcome Versus Process Simulations in Online Courses
declared.venue: International Journal of Cognitive Research in Science, Engineering and Education
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « Pham Taylor from thought to action process versus outcome based mental simulations » (2026-11-23)

population: 269 Saudi female undergraduates (Arabic first language) in online classes, randomly given process (139) or outcome (130) simulation

findings.text: Compared with picturing the good grade, rehearsing the steps made no difference to engagement, midterm test scores or predictions of performance

support.sentence: It did not influence behavioral engagement, midterm test performance, or predictions of performance before or after the test.

findings.text: The type of simulation changed assignment scores, in a way that depended on when the assignment was assessed

support.sentence: Type of simulation impacted students’ performance on assignments, but differently depending on the timing of the assessment.

findings.text: Assignments of the first half of the semester were better after picturing the good grade than after rehearsing the steps

support.sentence: Performance on assignments completed during the 1st half of the semester was higher for students who carried out the outcome simulation exercise, t(267) = 2.74, p = .006.
support.readBy: choose-your-struggle reviser, 2026-11-26: publisher PDF (ijcrsee.com, article 326), Results

limits: women only, one private university in Al Khobar; two short written exercises (5 questions), at the start of the semester and before the midterm
only process against outcome was randomized; the baseline is an earlier cohort matched on credits and grades, not randomized
several outcomes: the assignment effects go in opposite directions by half of the semester (outcome first, process second)
the outcome group imagined 5 actions after learning of a high mark: an outcome simulation, not an idealized fantasy as in Oettingen's work
small open-access journal (cited twice); online classes during the COVID-19 pandemic, summer 2020
an Arab sample (Saudi Arabia): the only one in this dossier on mental simulation
